notes.startup: demo/dist is committed, so `npm run build` returns immediately and `npm start` only serves files. Building the dashboard needs a full pnpm install plus ~20s of vite, which is more than a preview build step should risk. demo/server.mjs uses node builtins only, binds the assigned port straight away and needs no node_modules. Commands are invoked directly rather than through npm, because npm swallows unknown flags and would drop --port.
notes.externalDependencies: None. The preview runs the real agent dashboard with its axios transport replaced by an in-browser dataset (demo/transport.js), so no Rails, Postgres or Redis is involved. The full stack needs Ruby 3.4, Postgres with pgvector and Redis and is run locally with bin/local-dev.sh, not here.
notes.hashRouting: Routes live after the '#'. A preview engine serves the build from wherever it likes; with path routing the app only works when that is the origin root. ApiClient also reads the account id from the hash in this build (see vite.demo.config.ts).
